rationale: The base station auto-updated to firmware 4.5, which removed support for the legacy v2 radio protocol. The office camera (CAM-I2, fw 1.2) still speaks v2, and check_firmware_compat confirms no OTA upgrade path exists for this hardware revision (ota_available_to: null). Logs show E-305 "protocol v2 not supported" and "OTA unavailable for legacy hardware", matching the historical case H-03 that was escalated to FAE.

results.text: The peripheral firmware speaks a radio protocol the base station no longer supports, or vice versa. Frontline action: trigger OTA upgrade of the peripheral. If OTA is not available for the device or fails twice, escalate to FAE as protocol conflict.

results.source: historical_cases#H-03 Indoor camera lost after night update
results.text: After HB-200 auto-updated to 4.5, a CAM-I2 running 1.2 disconnected with E-305. OTA not offered for this hardware revision. Escalated; FAE confirmed protocol v2 dropped and arranged a compatibility firmware. Escalated correctly.

Base station firmware updates are pushed automatically at night. HB-200 firmware 4.5 removes support for the legacy v2 radio protocol. Peripherals still running v2 firmware must be upgraded to v3 firmware before or after the base station update, otherwise they disconnect.

complaint: My office camera no longer connects since the overnight base station update. I've tried to re-add it three times and each time it says it can't connect. It is the oldest camera I have, from the first package three years ago. The rest of the system is fine, so I'm hesitant to blame the update.
